NEW DELHI: Virat Kohli will have another major milestone in sight when India take on New Zealand in the first ODI at Eden Park in Auckland on Wednesday. The former India captain is closing in on a record held by legendary batter Sachin Tendulkar Kohli is currently the third-highest run-scorer among Indian batters in ODIs played in New Zealand. He has scored 514 runs in 11 matches on New Zealand soil and needs another 139 runs to move to the top of the list.Sachin Tendulkar is at the top of the list with 652 runs in 18 ODIs played in New Zealand. He scored one century (100 or more runs in an innings) and four half-centuries (50 to 99 runs). His highest score was 163 not out, which means he was not dismissed in that innings.Virender Sehwag is second with 598 runs in 12 matches. He scored three centuries and two half-centuries, with his highest score being 125 not out.Kohli, who occupies the third position with 514 runs in 11 matches, has scored one century and four half-centuries in New Zealand. His highest score is 123 runs.MS Dhoni is fourth on the list with 505 runs in 13 matches. He did not score a century but registered five half-centuries.His highest score was 84 not out.Rahul Dravid completes the top five with 425 runs in 12 matches. He scored one century and two half-centuries, with his highest score being 123 not out.Meanwhile, India captain Shubman Gill has confirmed the team's top four batters for the five-match ODI series against New Zealand.Gill said the top order would feature four right-handed batters - himself, Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer. The team will follow a flexible approach for the No. 5 and No. 6 positions, with KL Rahul and Axar Patel available depending on the situation."We will have a floating approach for No. 5 and No.6. Our top four is set, all right-handers. So if lefty is needed, Axar bhai goes and depending on match situation even KL bhai can go. So bit flexible," Gill said at the pre-match press conference ahead of the first ODI.India will begin their five-match ODI series against New Zealand in Auckland on November 4.
Article Summary: Sachin Tendulkar is top of the list with 652 runs in 18 ODIs played in New Zealand. Virender Sehwag is second with 598 runs in 12 matches. Virat Kohli, who occupies the third position with 514 runs in 11 matches. India captain Shubman Gill has confirmed the team's top four batters for the five-match ODI series.

Article Title: Tusshar Kapoor gets Rs 5 crore extortion threat in name of Bishnoi gang; police suspect impersonator
Article Text:
Tusshar Kapoor received an extortion call demanding Rs 5 crore from someone posing as a gang member





MUMBAI: Bollywood actor Tusshar Kapoor allegedly received an extortion call demanding Rs 5 crore from a person claiming to be Harry Boxer, a member of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang.However, a preliminary investigation by the Mumbai Crime Branch has ruled out the involvement of Bishnoi gang members in the threat call.Tusshar has informally alerted the Mumbai Police about the threat, following which his security has been beefed up. The investigation has been handed over to the Crime Branch and its Anti-Extortion Cell.According to police sources, the Crime Branch’s technical team examined the audio recording of the threatening call and compared the sender’s voice with official audio samples of Harry Boxer available in its database.The analysis reportedly found no match between the two recordings.Police suspect that an unidentified person may have impersonated a Bishnoi gang member and used the gang’s name to intimidate the actor and extort money.No First Information Report (FIR) has been registered so far, as the police are continuing their investigation to establish the origin of the audio recording and identify the caller.
Article Summary: Bollywood actor Tusshar Kapoor allegedly received an extortion call demanding Rs 5 crore from a person claiming to be Harry Boxer. A preliminary investigation by the Mumbai Crime Branch has ruled out the involvement of Bishnoi gang members in the threat call.

NEW DELHI: West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh on Tuesday criticised former chief minister Mamata Banerjee for attending the INDIA bloc rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Taking a dig at Mamata, he said that she was turning to Congress leader Sonia Gandhi for leadership out of "utter helplessness".Ghosh claimed that Banerjee's party has lost political ground in its state and that she was seeking political relevance by aligning with the Congress leadership.“Earlier, she set out to become the top leader herself. Now, she has nothing left in her hands. Today, she isn’t even an elected representative. That is why, out of utter helplessness, she goes around accepting Sonia ji as her leader again. Her party is finished today,” news agency ANI reported, quoting Ghosh.He also hit out at Banerjee over her objections to the electoral process, saying political parties must respect the people's mandate. He alleged that she had no complaints about the Election Commission or democracy when her party was winning elections.“As long as she was winning, democracy was fine, and the Election Commission was fine. The moment she lost, everything went wrong. Keep faith in the people; the people decide who wins and who loses. One must accept the verdict of the public,” he said.The minister further claimed that the removal of fake voters during the electoral roll revision had paved the way for free and fair elections in West Bengal. He alleged that Banerjee had benefited from such voters in previous elections.“Look, when the revision occurred, the fake voter base through which Mamata used to win was eliminated. Once they were separated, a free and fair election took place. A genuine election happened in Bengal after many years, and people are happy about it; change has arrived. No outsider can simply enter and become a citizen of this country or avail benefits here,” he said.Ghosh also said the ruling government and party workers would organise rallies across the state to counter the Opposition's attempts to create unrest and communicate their position to the public.“It is also our responsibility to make people understand and deliver the right message. The people are nationalist, and the government is nationalist. No one will be permitted to create unrest in the country. We will also reach out to the people and hold rallies everywhere; this is just the beginning,” he said.Meanwhile, Ghosh said the state government was making arrangements to ensure that Deepavali, Kali Puja and Jagaddhatri Puja celebrations passed off peacefully.He said every cabinet minister had been assigned a district to oversee law and order during the festive season. Ghosh has been given responsibility for Purba Medinipur, also known as East Midnapore.“The government is keeping a close watch across all of West Bengal to ensure that the upcoming Deepavali, Kali Puja, and Jagaddhatri Puja are conducted smoothly and with enthusiasm. Every cabinet minister has been assigned the responsibility of overseeing law and order in one district. I have been given charge of Purba Medinipur (East Midnapore). I am also meeting with them to ensure all arrangements are in place and nothing goes wrong. This is the government’s duty, and the public must cooperate,” he said.The minister also criticised the previous Trinamool Congress government over the functioning of development boards set up for marginalised communities, including the Matua community.He alleged that several boards formed during Banerjee's tenure had not received adequate funds or been given meaningful work.“Mamata Banerjee had formed several development boards in West Bengal: the Rajbanshi Board, the Matua Board, the Bhumij Adivasi Board, but gave neither funds nor work to anyone. She only played politics,” he said.Ghosh said the Matua community, many of whose members migrated from Bangladesh, continued to face economic hardships and needed focused development measures. He said the board should be made functional and provided with funds.“Now, for that community, especially the Matua community, most of whom came from Bangladesh, have numerous hardships and are poor. Their development must happen; therefore, the board must be actively functional for them, and funds must be provided, which our chief minister (Suvendu Adhikari) has initiated," he said.
Article Summary: West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh criticised former chief minister Mamata Banerjee for attending the INDIA bloc rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Ghosh claimed that Banerée's party has lost political ground in its state and that she was seeking political relevance by aligning with the Congress leadership.

Article Title: 'Air fares up by 700%': Don't fly, says SC
Article Text:
SC refuses urgent hearing on plea against steep rise in domestic airfares ahead of Diwali

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday refused to urgently list a plea against steep rise in domestic air fares during Diwali season and seeking a direction to Centre to frame a mechanism to cap air fares on domestic routes during festival periods.The issue of regulation of air fares is still pending before SC, a bench hearing the plea was informed while seeking the court's intervention. But the court turned down the plea.Advocate Abhinav for the petitioner submitted that fares have gone up 700% amounts to a violation of Article 14 of the Constitution. "Don't travel by air," the bench said.Centre had earlier told SC that the rules on air fares under Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024, will be published in two weeks.
Article Summary: Supreme Court refuses to urgently list a plea against steep rise in domestic air fares during Diwali season. The issue of regulation of air fares is still pending before SC. Centre had earlier told SC that the rules on air fares under Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam will be published in two weeks.

NEW DELHI: The Indian Navy has rescued all 20 crew members of a fishing vessel from armed pirates after a 48-hour operation in the Arabian Sea. The vessel, Azini, was reportedly seized by the armed pirates more than 3,000 km from Mumbai.Defence minister Rajnath Singh praised the Indian Navy for executing the meticulously coordinated 48-hour operation with support from the Indian Air Force. “The swift localisation, interception and safe release of the crew and vessel from significantly-armed pirates, with timely support from the IAF, speak well of the Indian Navy’s high operational readiness and ability to respond decisively to maritime threats across the region,” Rajnath said.A photograph shared by the minister on his post on X shows destroyer INS Kolkata standing by as heavily armed commandos guard what appear to be the pirates, seated on the deck of the fishing vessel. A huge cache of seized weapons was also seen lying on the vessel.“Our brave personnel have once again demonstrated India’s ability, intent and resolve to safeguard lives, uphold maritime security and ensure stability across the Indian Ocean Region.India continues to stand resolute in ensuring SAFE SEAS and a free, open and secure IOR,” he said.Monday’s operation was launched much further than the Navy's landmark anti-piracy mission of March 2024. The same destroyer had then intercepted the pirate ship MV Ruen around 2,600km from the Indian coast.The Indian Navy has deployed over 10 warships for anti-piracy and regional security operations like Operation Sankalp to patrol the Arabian Sea, Gulf of Aden, and the East Coast of Africa.Indian Navy has been proactively engaging with the regional and extra-regional navies and maritime forces, to promote maritime security. Since 2008, Indian Navy has deployed units in the Gulf of Aden and East Coast of Africa towards anti-piracy patrols.

Article Title: 'Azam the, Azam hain': Will the Khan factor help or haunt Akhilesh in 2027 UP elections?
Article Text:
The SP chief’s public show of support for the veteran leader comes amid questions over the Azam Khan family’s influence on the party’s prospects ahead of the 2027 elections.

Azam the, Azam hain aur Azam rahenge"

Azam was, Azam is and Azam will remain

The brief freedom

Azam Khan’s rise in SP was closely tied to his long-standing association with Mulayam Singh Yadav.

Akhilesh turns arrest into political battle

The Muslim vote and the Owaisi challenge

Muslims account for at least 30% of the population in around 70 constituencies.

Owaisi has attacked Akhilesh Yadav over the treatment of Azam Khan's family.

From kingmaker to political liability?

BJP's counter: 'Mafia raj' and law and order

UP accused Akhilesh of opposing Azam Khan’s release out of concern that the veteran leader could challenge his position in party.

NEW DELHI: ").With that emphatic declaration, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav sought to end speculation about his equation with one of the party's tallest Muslim leaders. But the political reality surrounding Mohammad Azam Khan is far more complicated than the slogan suggests.Nine days after Akhilesh's October 22 visit to Azam at Rampur jail, the veteran leader walked out of prison with his son Abdullah Azam after the Allahabad high court granted them bail in the dual PAN card case. His freedom, however, lasted barely minutes. The Enforcement Directorate arrested him in a separate money-laundering case linked to Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, and a court subsequently remanded him to 14 days' judicial custody.The dramatic turn has put Akhilesh's declaration to the test. Once among the most powerful figures in the SP, Azam remains central to the party's political calculations in Rampur and its relationship with Muslim voters. But his legal battles, the erosion of his family's electoral stronghold and the growing challenge from Asaduddin Owaisi have turned his return into a complicated political proposition.As Uttar Pradesh heads towards the 2027 assembly election, Akhilesh faces a question that goes beyond personal loyalty: can he hold on to Azam's political legacy without becoming hostage to its baggage?Azam and Abdullah had been in custody since November 2025 following their conviction in the dual PAN card case.The Allahabad high court's order suspended their 10-year sentences and granted them bail, paving the way for their release.However, the ED had a separate case waiting. The agency arrested Azam shortly after he walked out of Rampur jail, while Abdullah was allowed to go home.The money-laundering investigation relates to alleged financial irregularities in the construction of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur. The ED has alleged that government funds were diverted for the university's construction. Azam is the founder of the university and heads the trust that runs it. These are allegations being investigated by the agency, not findings of guilt in the present case.Speaking to reporters after his release, Azam alleged that he was being punished for being a Muslim and for establishing a university and schools. "What is there left to say? What can I say? The law has ceased to exist. Is this the punishment for being a Muslim?" he said.The following day, a special PMLA court in Ghaziabad sent him to 14 days' judicial custody. The court proceedings ensured that the brief release did not translate into a return to political activity.Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav responded sharply to the ED action, accusing the BJP government of using cases to repeatedly send an elderly political leader to jail.In a post on X, the SP chief said: "Let today's rulers remember that thrones change when the time changes. The conspiracy being hatched against Mr Azam Khan through these cases is being watched not just by the entire country, but by the whole world."He added that repeatedly implicating an elderly man in cases and sending him to jail was "an utterly cowardly act", warning that injustice could eventually turn into a calamity for those responsible.The response was significant because it came barely nine days after Akhilesh had visited Azam in jail. That meeting had already signalled that the SP chief was unwilling to distance himself from the veteran leader despite the legal controversies surrounding him.The ED arrest has now sharpened the political messaging. For Akhilesh, the issue is no longer simply Azam's return to the party's political fold. It is also about positioning the SP against what it describes as the misuse of investigative agencies to target opposition leaders.The BJP, on the other hand, has defended the ED action, maintaining that the law applies equally to everyone.For the Samajwadi Party, the stakes in the Azam Khan question go well beyond the fortunes of one leader. They concern the party's hold over a crucial section of its traditional support base: Muslim voters. Muslims account for roughly 19% of Uttar Pradesh's population, making them one of the state's largest voting blocs. Their concentration in several constituencies gives them considerable electoral influence. In the 2022 assembly election, the community was a decisive factor in around 70 constituencies where Muslims formed at least 30% of the population.The 2022 results also showed how strongly the community rallied behind the SP. The party fielded 64 Muslim candidates, of whom 31 won, taking the total number of Muslim MLAs in the assembly to 36, up from 24 in 2017. The BSP fielded 88 Muslim candidates and the Congress 75, while AIMIM fielded more than 60. Yet neither the BSP nor Congress managed to elect a single Muslim MLA. The results suggested that the SP had emerged as the principal beneficiary of Muslim consolidation, even as smaller parties remained relevant in individual constituencies.Azam Khan was central to this political equation. His influence in Rampur and his standing among sections of the Muslim community gave the SP an important local and regional network. His electoral record, along with that of his wife Tazeen Fatima and son Abdullah Azam, made the family one of the most prominent Muslim political establishments in the state. His absence from active politics has therefore left a space that other political players may seek to occupy.It is this space that AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi is attempting to enter. His October 18 rally in Tanda was a reminder that the SP cannot take Muslim support for granted. Owaisi accused Akhilesh of treating Muslims as a vote bank while prioritising the Yadav community, and questioned why the SP leadership had not done more for Azam Khan. His pitch was for independent Muslim political representation, arguing that the community should produce its own MLAs and MPs rather than remain a support base for established political families.Owaisi's intervention is significant because the SP's electoral arithmetic depends not just on retaining Muslim support but also on preventing its fragmentation. The 2022 results showed the limits of smaller parties: although BSP and AIMIM fielded substantial numbers of Muslim candidates, neither managed to convert that presence into Muslim representation in the Assembly. However, even without winning seats, such parties can potentially affect the outcome in closely contested constituencies by splitting votes.Akhilesh's October 22 visit to Azam in Rampur jail was therefore also a political signal. His declaration, "Azam they, Azam hain aur Azam rahenge" (Azam was, is and will remain), aimed to reassure the veteran leader's followers that the SP had not abandoned him. The visit came amid growing questions over whether Owaisi could use sympathy for Azam to make inroads among Muslim voters.The challenge is compounded by the SP's wider social coalition strategy. Akhilesh has sought to move beyond the traditional Muslim-Yadav combination through his PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) framework, bringing backward classes, Dalits and minorities under a broader political umbrella. But the party cannot afford to lose its Muslim support base while attempting to expand its reach among other communities.As the 2027 assembly election approaches, Akhilesh faces a delicate balancing act. He must reassure Azam's supporters that the SP continues to value the veteran leader and his political legacy, while ensuring that the party's Muslim support base does not become an opening for Owaisi or other rivals. The 2022 election demonstrated the electoral value of Muslim consolidation behind the SP. The question now is whether Akhilesh can hold that coalition together without relying too heavily on one leader or one political family.To understand Akhilesh Yadav's dilemma, one must first understand the extent of Azam Khan's influence in Rampur. For decades, Khan was not just the Samajwadi Party's most powerful face in the district but the man who dominated its political landscape. He challenged the influence of Rampur's erstwhile Nawab family and gradually built a formidable political network, winning the Rampur Sadar assembly seat 10 times. His influence extended beyond his own electoral victories: his wife, Tazeen Fatima, succeeded him as MLA in a 2019 bypoll, while his son Abdullah Azam twice won the Suar assembly seat. The Azam family's political presence became so entrenched that Rampur's electoral fortunes were often seen through the prism of Khan's influence.That hold was not easily broken. In the 2022 assembly election, Azam Khan won Rampur Sadar for the 10th time despite campaigning from jail. The BJP's Akash Saxena, one of his most prominent political adversaries who had pursued several cases against Azam Khan and his family, lost that contest. But the equation changed after Khan was disqualified following his conviction in a hate speech case. In the December 2022 bypoll, Saxena defeated Azam Khan's close aide Asim Raza by around 34,000 votes, delivering the BJP its first victory in Rampur Sadar and making Saxena the first Hindu candidate to win the constituency. The result marked a significant breach in a political stronghold that Khan and his family had dominated for decades.The erosion of the Azam family's influence became more apparent in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. With Khan, his wife and son facing imprisonment, the SP fielded Maulana Mohibullah Nadvi from Rampur. The choice reportedly upset Khan's loyalists, many of whom stayed away from campaigning, exposing a growing rift between the local Azam camp and the party leadership. It was a reminder that Azam Khan's network could still matter to the SP even in his absence, but also that Akhilesh could no longer assume the family would automatically fall in line with the party's decisions.His treatment by the central agencies gives the party an opportunity to frame the issue as one of political targeting and due process. But the party will have to contend with the electoral consequences of being closely associated with a leader whose legal record has become a recurring political flashpoint.The challenge for Akhilesh is to retain the political value of the Azam network without allowing the controversies surrounding Khan and his family to define the SP's wider campaign. In Rampur, the question is no longer simply whether Azam Khan can return to politics. It is whether the political machinery he built can still deliver for the Samajwadi Party, and on whose terms.In 2022, UP CM Yogi Adityanath famously said: "Even Akhilesh doesn’t want Azam Khan to come out of jail because it will pose a threat to his position [chair]. The state government has nothing to do with these cases, whether they are related to Azam Khan or anyone else. It is the court that grants bail.""Under previous governments, mafias were running a parallel administration. When we took action against the land mafia who grabbed poor farmers' land for private universities and personal fiefdoms, the Samajwadi Party developed sympathy for criminals instead of the victims," he had said.The above remarks are at the core of the BJP's attack.The BJP has consistently used the Azam Khan issue to attack the Samajwadi Party's record on law and order. The party's broader political narrative has sought to associate the SP's previous tenure with alleged criminal influence and what it describes as 'mafia raj'.That gives the BJP an obvious line of attack if Akhilesh makes Azam's rehabilitation a central political theme. The ruling party can frame the SP's outreach as evidence that it has not moved away from its past.The SP, meanwhile, has to navigate the distinction between allegations, court findings and the political narrative built around them. It can point to the legal process and the need for due process, but it cannot wish away the electoral impact of the cases and convictions.The BJP's attack also puts the SP's broader coalition strategy under pressure. Akhilesh has sought to expand the party's social base beyond its traditional support groups through the PDA framework. A campaign dominated by the Azam Khan controversy could complicate that effort.Akhilesh's jail visit, his response to the ED arrest and the party's continued engagement with Azam Khan send a message to the SP's traditional supporters: the party has not abandoned a leader who played a major role in building its political presence.But the message also carries risks. The SP has to decide how much political space to give the Azam family, how prominently to project its association with them and how to prevent the issue from becoming a defining feature of its 2027 campaign.For Akhilesh, the Azam question will ultimately be about the political arithmetic as much as loyalty. He needs to reassure sections of the Muslim electorate that the SP remains attentive to their concerns, while keeping the PDA coalition broad enough to bring together backward classes, Dalits and minorities.As Uttar Pradesh moves towards 2027, Akhilesh's tightrope walk will be to retain the political value of an old ally without inheriting all the baggage that comes with him. Azam may be an asset the SP cannot easily discard, but he may also turn out to be a liability the party cannot afford to let define its next election.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav's public show of support for the veteran leader comes amid questions over the Azam Khan family's influence on the party's prospects ahead of the 2027 elections. Azam's rise in SP was closely tied to his long-standing association with Mulayam Singh Yadav. His legal battles, the erosion of his family's electoral stronghold and the growing challenge from Asaduddin Owaisi have turned his return into a political proposition.

Article Title: EC can't monopolise voter awareness campaigns: SC; sets aside order denying permission to civil society
Article Text:
Voter awareness not EC's monopoly, says SC; sets aside SEC order

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday said Election Commission did not have a monopoly over conducting ‘voter awareness campaigns” while disapproving EC’s refusal to permit a civil society group led by Aruna Roy from running a campaign to educate voters to choose representatives carefully and not barter their votes for bribes.Setting aside Rajasthan State Election Commission’s Oct 9 refusing permission for the civil society in this regard, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana gave 48 hours to the SEC to consider their representation to run voter awareness campaigns for the final phase of Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti elections scheduled for Nov 14.SEC, through advocate Amit Kuri, said permission was refused keeping in mind the imposition of prohibitory orders for maintenance of law and order situation before the elections to keep at bay unwanted and anti-social elements.Roy’s counsel Prashant Bhushan said it is a voter awareness campaign and not political activity and questioned the legitimacy of blanket imposition of prohibitory orders under Section 163 of BNSS to prohibit congregation for any political purpose.The bench told SEC that EC conducting voter awareness programmes does not mean others are prohibited from doing similar exercises. “In the event they do or indulge in any corrupt practices, you are there to rectify it.But you cannot monopolise voter awareness campaigns. Everyone has a right to do so.”SC turned to Bhushan and said civil society cannot give a general application seeking permission to carry out voter awareness campaigns and said it must specify the place and time for conducting such exercise to the authorities concerned for permission.SC issued notice to Rajasthan SEC, set aside its Oct 9 order refusing permission and directed it “to reconsider the petitioners’ request for permitting them to conduct voter awareness campaign during the phase 3 of the Panchayati raj elections.”While the final phase of voting would end on Nov 14, the election of ‘sarpanchs’ and ‘panchs’ is scheduled for Nov 16. The three-phase elections covered 41 Zila Parishads, 457 Panchayat Samitis and 14,403 Gram Panchayats.
Article Summary: Supreme Court sets aside Rajasthan State Election Commission’s Oct 9 refusing permission for the civil society in this regard. Justices gave 48 hours to the SEC to consider their representation to run voter awareness campaigns for the final phase of Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti elections scheduled for Nov 14.

Article Title: Marital discord no ground for termination of pregnancy: SC
Article Text:
Supreme Court seeks reconciliation between estranged couple as it hears woman's plea to terminate over six-month pregnancy, opposed by her husband

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday found itself in a predicament on an abortion plea of a woman who sought its approval for termination of her over-six-month pregnancy over the discord with her husband, who opposed the plea on the ground that he also has a right over the unborn child.A bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan said that termination of pregnancy can be allowed in case of rape and sexual assault or if there is some problem with the foetus, but a case like the present one stood on a different footing. It questioned where society would be headed if a woman could decide to abort on the ground that she was ill-treated or abused by her husband and in-laws.Stating that the child in the womb is because of love and the father has also a right over the unborn child, SC tried to pacify the petitioner to persuade her not to insist on abortion as the foetus is in a healthy condition. "It is normal that wife talks against husband and husband talks against wife but it does not mean that you have to terminate the pregnancy on that ground. It is not a case of sexual assault or single woman becoming pregnant. Where are we heading as a society if the wife says that she wants termination of pregnancy because of her fight with the husband and in-laws... What about the right of the father."The petitioner, with whom the bench interacted virtually, said she did not want to carry the pregnancy and she wanted a divorce.But the husband said that he will take the child after birth and will care and pleaded with the court not to allow termination.As the bone of contention which sparked the feud was the man's allegation about her character, the bench asked him to first file an affidavit before it to withdraw all allegations as a first step towards rapprochement. It posted the case for Wednesday.
Article Summary: Supreme Court hears woman's plea to terminate over six-month pregnancy, opposed by her husband. Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan said that termination of pregnancy can be allowed in case of rape and sexual assault or if there is some problem with the foetus.

Article Title: First in 47 years: No operational fatality in CRPF in an entire year
Article Text:
CRPF records a year without operational fatalities for the first time in 47 years, with its last such death reported on October 30, 2025

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: CRPF has, for the first time in 47 years, completed a year without sustaining a single operational fatality; this, despite its personnel having been engaged in several high-risk operations during this period across violence-hit theatres like Jammu and Kashmir, Left-wing extremism-hit areas and Manipur."A significant milestone in the history of CRPF -- 12 consecutive months have passed without any operational fatality in the force, the last operational fatality...being on Oct 30, 2025," CRPF DG G P Singh posted on X on Monday.He credited the "milestone" to "latest & contemporary hardware, better training & strategic planning along with focus on post-incident response including high speed evacuation of injured personnel to secondary and tertiary medical facilities"."It’s especially significant since this has happened while we continue to be deployed and engage intensely in all the major operational theatres achieving significant breakthrough results," said Singh.In the past year, CRPF personnel led the decisive battle against Left-wing extremism in 2026, hitting Maoists in their pocket boroughs and eliminating their top leadership. The country was declared ‘Naxal free’ in March 2026.In Manipur, CRPF is deployed since ethnic violence broke out there in May 2023. The state continues to face bouts of violence, many over the past one year.J&K too has seen sustained anti-terror operations in the past 12 months.Since 1947, 2,268 CRPF personnel have been killed in operations, averaging at over 28 fatalities a year. Between 1947 and 2026, the CRPF suffered a maximum 143 fatalities in 2010, essentially on account of a Maoist ambush that left 75 CRPF personnel dead.A senior CRPF official said the absence of fatalities is the result of conscious efforts and course-correction. Apart from providing the best protective gear and equipment to personnel, there is in-depth planning of every operation. Normal and routine administrative movements are treated on par with operational movements in high-risk areas and similar precautions taken. Also, 1.5 times the required force is deployed in each operation. "That is how there was not a single casualty during Operation Black Forest in Kareguttalu Hills last year, even as 21 Naxalites were killed," said an officer.Following a post-analysis of the fatalities in CRPF, it was found that 3/4th to 4/5th of fatalities follow days after injury. "It was obvious that timely medical care could prevent such fatalities. Now, thanks to MHA, air-ambulances routinely airlift injured personnel to secondary and tertiary hospitals without delay, giving them better chances at survival," said the officer.Interestingly, G P Singh had, during his stint as Assam DGP before he became CRPF DG, achieved the same feat, having brought down operational fatalities in the state police to zero in 2023.This is the sixth time-stretch since 1947 when the CRPF recorded nil casualties. The last such period had lasted 24 months, from Feb 1977 and Jan 1979.
Article Summary: CRPF records a year without operational fatalities for the first time in 47 years, with its last such death reported on October 30, 2025. Since 1947, 2,268 CRPF personnel have been killed in operations, averaging at over 28 fatalities a year. This is the sixth time-stretch since 1947 when the CRPF recorded nil casualties.

NEW DELHI: With homebuyers continuing to face years of delays in getting possession of their homes despite RERA’s enactment, pan-India homebuyers’ body FPCE has urged PM Narendra Modi to overhaul the law by separating consumer protection from real estate sector promotion. It has flagged an inherent conflict between the two objectives of RERA and persistent enforcement failures by regulators.Flagging how different RERAs across states are giving priority to promotion of real estate sector over playing stricter regulatory role to bring relief to buyers, Abhay Upadhyay, a member of govt’s advisory council for RERA and FPCE has urged govt to separate “promotion from protection” and re-enact RERA as “Real Estate Homebuyers Protection Act”.This comes as govt prepares to amend the law that was enacted in 2016 with the promise to end delay in completion of projects and protect consumers’ interest. FPCE has suggested bringing in an effective accountability framework so that repeated failures to enforce statutory provisions or pass arbitrary orders, prevent violations and executive orders do not continue without scrutiny or consequences.

NEW DELHI: The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) has completed 12 consecutive months without losing any personnel in operational fatalities, marking an achievement not recorded in the force in 47 years.CRPF Director General GP Singh congratulated personnel on the milestone, saying the last operational death in the force was recorded on October 30, 2025. The previous time the CRPF went such a long period without an operational fatality was before January 1979.Sharing the achievement on X, Singh wrote, “A significant milestone in the history of CRPF - 12 consecutive months (One Year) have passed without any Operational fatality in the force, the last operational fatality in the force being on Oct 30th 2025. This has happened after 47 Years (last such period ended in January 1979).”He attributed the achievement to improvements in equipment, training and operational planning. The force's focus on responding quickly to incidents, particularly by evacuating injured personnel to secondary and tertiary medical facilities, had also played an important role, he said.“It’s especially significant since this has happened while we continue to be deployed and engage intensely in all the major operational theatres, achieving significant breakthrough results.We remain committed to keeping the country peaceful & safe for all its citizens,” wrote the CRPF D-G.However, the milestone comes against the backdrop of another serious challenge facing the force, the rising number of personnel dying by suicide. Such deaths are recorded separately from fatalities during security operations.In August, the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) took suo motu cognisance of a media report stating that 19 CRPF personnel had died by suicide in less than five months, between January and May 2026.The Commission observed that the reported deaths, if true, raised serious concerns about the right to life of personnel serving in the country's largest Central Armed Police Force. It issued notices to the Union Home Secretary and the CRPF Director General, seeking detailed reports on the matter.According to the media report published on August 11, a total of 281 CRPF personnel died by suicide over the previous five years, of whom around 216 were on duty.The force recorded 57 suicides in 2021, 43 in 2022, 57 in 2023, 46 in 2024 and 59 in 2025. The 59 deaths recorded last year were reportedly the highest annual toll from suicides in the five-year period.

Article Title: 'Your social media posts amounted to instigation': Bombay HC pulls up actor Imran Khan - top quotes
Article Text:
'Your social media posts amounted to instigation': Bombay HC told actor Imran Khan.

Here's what court said:

"If an Indian had done the same thing elsewhere would it have been tolerated? If this had happened in America, the person would have been put on the next flight back to India," the high court remarked, suggesting Khan to consider taking Indian citizenship if he was so keen on participating in protests.

The court said while it was not disputing the powers of the authorities to take such an action (to issue notice), certain ground realities also need to be considered.

"He (Khan) is ready to tender an unconditional apology. He has been in India since childhood. Show some magnanimity and a big heart now. We have to be 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (the world is one family)," the court said.

As far as law is concerned, the authorities have sovereign powers, the court said, adding they would be well within their powers to deport the actor.

"As an OCI cardholder, you (Khan) are at the mercy of this country. Hence, such behaviour cannot be tolerated, but one chance can be given," the high court said.

For what had he (Khan) gone to a place of protest (in Mumbai)? the bench asked while adding in a lighter vein that the actor does not even have any film coming up to promote.

"The rights Indian citizens enjoy and the rights available to OCI cardholders are different. If he had been an Indian citizen then the situation would have been different," Chief Justice Tripathi noted .

Khan holds an OCI card and hence he cannot behave like an Indian citizen, the bench further said.

"You (Khan) had no right to participate in a protest of such nature. You have no connection with the SIR (Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls undertaken by EC). The right to protest is not available to an OCI cardholder," HC said.

NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court on Monday pulled up actor Imran Khan, a US citizen holding an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card, for taking part in a protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The court observed that the right to protest was available only to Indian citizens, after which the actor tendered an unconditional apology.A bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna remarked that instead of deporting Khan immediately, authorities had shown leniency by issuing him a notice asking him to leave the country.Khan's lawyer, Venkatesh Dhond, responded by submitting an undertaking that the 43-year-old actor would not participate in any protest in the future. He also conveyed Khan's unconditional apology to the court.The actor had approached the high court challenging a notice issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO), directing him to leave India by October 28. The notice followed his participation in a protest over the SIR exercise in Mumbai last month.The bench posted the matter for further hearing on December 7 and extended its earlier order keeping the FRRO notice in abeyance until then.The court also reiterated that an OCI cardholder does not have the right to participate in protests in India.Senior counsel Venkatesh Dhond, appearing for Khan, initially submitted an undertaking to the court on the actor's behalf, assuring that he would neither participate in any future protest nor instigate others to do so.However, the court said the undertaking alone would not be enough and asked Khan to tender an unconditional apology.The court observed that Khan had been in India since childhood, had worked in the film industry here and had earned recognition in the country."Your social media posts (after he was released from detention by police) amounted to instigation. You have young followers who are bound to get influenced," it said.The Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) had issued the 'Leave India' order under Sections 7(2)(C) and 29 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act. These provisions empower the government to restrict the movement of foreign nationals and enforce their removal from the country.The notice directed Khan to leave India by October 28, warning that deportation proceedings would be initiated if he failed to comply.The action followed Khan's brief detention by police during a demonstration at Mumbai's historic August Kranti Maidan on October 10. The rally was held in solidarity with an agitation by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.In his petition challenging the FRRO notice, filed through advocate Zulfiquar Memon, Khan maintained that he had not participated in the gathering and had no association or affiliation with its organisers.
Article Summary: Imran Khan, a US citizen holding an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card, was ordered to leave India by October 28. The actor had taken part in a protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The court observed that the right to protest was available only to Indian citizens, after which the actor tendered an unconditional apology.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Steffi Graf had won 22 Grand Slam titles and spent years dominating women's tennis. Yet one of her most emotional moments came away from the court. During her 2004 International Tennis Hall of Fame induction, her husband, Andre Agassi, took the stage to introduce her. What followed was more than a tribute to a tennis champion. His heartfelt words about their relationship left Graf wiping away tears.Agassi did not spend his speech listing her records or celebrating her trophies. Instead, the eight-time Grand Slam champion spoke about the woman behind the achievements. He praised her character, her ability to overcome difficult moments and the life they had built together. Graf later responded with an equally touching message.The moment took place in 2004 when Graf entered the International Tennis Hall of Fame. Agassi had the honour of introducing his wife, and he made it clear that finding the right words to describe her was not easy."As I attempt to find words worthy to introduce the person that has changed my life, I realize the words have yet to be invented that are large enough, colorful enough, or true enough to express the heart and soul of this woman that I love," Agassi said during his introduction speech.He then spoke about how Graf never allowed her tennis achievements to define her as a person."You have never defined yourself by what you have achieved; rather, you have achieved by how you defined yourself," he said.Agassi also admired how she approached life after retiring from professional tennis in 1999. For him, her decision to embrace motherhood and family life showed the same dedication she had displayed throughout her playing career."And even now, it has taken my breath away to see how you've quietly laid down your racket to pursue love and motherhood, with the same zeal and high standards you have always demanded of yourself," he added.However, his tribute did not stop there. Agassi also remembered Graf's ability to overcome adversity, play through injuries and return to winning ways."The history books will record for posterity, your ability to embrace and rise above adversity, to play through injury, and to win again, and again, and again," he said.Graf had been wiping away tears throughout the ceremony. Hearing her husband speak about her beyond her achievements made the occasion even more personal.When Graf stepped forward to accept the honour, she had a special message for Agassi. Rather than simply thanking him for the introduction, she spoke about what meeting him had meant to her."Not that this occasion isn't emotional enough, to hear how much you are loved is amazing," Graf said during her acceptance speech.She then looked towards her husband and delivered one of the most touching lines of the ceremony."The best part of the tour is I ran into you. I'll be forever grateful for that," she added.Agassi saved his biggest declaration for the end of his introduction. He spoke about the impact Graf had made on him and their family."We have been touched deeply by your life, you have made us better, and we will never be the same," he said.He then introduced her as "the greatest person I've ever known."The couple had married in October 2001 and welcomed their son, Jaden, that same year. Their daughter, Jaz, was born in 2003. Their relationship had also grown beyond their shared tennis careers, giving Agassi another reason to admire the woman he had introduced that day.Seven years after Graf's induction, Agassi also entered the International Tennis Hall of Fame in 2011. Together, they have won 30 Grand Slam singles titles. Yet their 2004 ceremony offered something no trophy could capture: a public reminder of how deeply two tennis champions valued each other.
Article Summary: Steffi Graf was inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame in 2004. Her husband, Andre Agassi, took the stage to introduce her. His heartfelt words about their relationship left Graf wiping away tears. Graf later responded with an equally touching message.

A 20-year-old co-pilot aboard a Learjet that crashed in Florida, killing all nine people on board, texted her pilot boyfriend just minutes before the deadly accident, her family has revealed.Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras was in touch with her loved ones and air traffic control until the aircraft plunged to the ground in Palm Beach County on Sunday afternoon.Her stepfather, Thiago Corteleti, told the New York Post that Filgueiras had messaged her boyfriend, also a pilot, around 12:40 pm, just 10 minutes before the crash at approximately 12:50 pm."She just said, 'I've got turbulence, I've got ice,'" Corteleti told, recalling the message she sent to her boyfriend.Her co-pilot on Sunday's flight has not yet been identified. Article Title: 'The Big Show' is over: Glenn Maxwell announces retirement from international cricket

Australian all-rounder Glenn Maxwell has announced his retirement from international cricket, bringing an end to a career in which he entertained fans with his aggressive batting and unusual shots. Maxwell made the announcement on Tuesday during an episode of The Final Word podcast. His decision also includes his retirement from domestic 50-over and four-day cricket for Victoria.Maxwell, popularly known as 'The Big Show', represented Australia in 149 ODIs, 130 T20Is and seven Test matches. He was part of Australia's 2015 and 2023 ODI World Cup-winning teams and also played a key role in the team's T20 World Cup triumph in 2021."I'm going to be announcing my retirement from international cricket and domestic games for Victoria in the 50 over and the four-day stuff, red ball completely," the 38-year-old told The Final Word podcast in an episode released on Tuesday.Maxwell said he wants to give more attention to his fitness and prepare his body for the remaining tournaments in his career."It's probably a time where I probably need to spend a little bit more time investing in the body to make sure I can get through the remaining couple of tournaments I've got in my career."He scored 3,990 runs in ODIs and 2,897 runs in T20 internationals. His last appearance for Australia came against Oman at the T20 World Cup in Sri Lanka in February.Maxwell also made a special mark in T20 cricket. Along with India's Rohit Sharma, he remains one of only two players to score five international centuries in the format.With his off-spin bowling, he also picked up 128 wickets for Australia in the two shorter formats.Maxwell had retired from ODI cricket last year but was hoping to play one final international match at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG).However, that possibility ended when Australia announced its squad for the upcoming series against England on Monday. The selectors have focused on younger players in their short-format plans.Maxwell admitted that he had hoped to get a farewell match at his home ground but understood the team's decision."There was, I suppose, a small hope or discussion that I might have been able to potentially get a send-off game at the MCG, but I can completely understand the direction they're going with this squad," he said.

Article Title: Steffi Graf at 57: Behind 22 Grand Slam titles lies a story of pressure, heartbreak and sacrifice
Article Text:
Steffi Graf (Getty Images)

Steffi Graf's tennis career was shaped by extraordinary pressure

Steffi Graf chose family and charity after retirement

At 57, Steffi Graf remains one of the most celebrated names in tennis history. Her achievements still set her apart, from 22 Grand Slam singles titles to an extraordinary 377 weeks at world No. 1. Yet her legacy is not only about records. Graf's career brought intense pressure, public attention and difficult personal moments. After years spent competing at the highest level, she stepped away from professional tennis and built a life that placed family and personal priorities ahead of the spotlight.Graf became a professional player at just 13. Her rise was rapid, and the expectations grew with every major victory. She eventually reached the top of women's tennis and delivered one of the sport's rarest achievements in 1988, winning all four Grand Slam singles titles and Olympic gold in the same calendar year. That historic Golden Slam remains a defining moment in tennis.But success came with a demanding schedule and constant public attention. Her family also faced difficult scrutiny, including the tax-evasion case involving her father, Peter Graf.In 1993, tennis was shaken by the stabbing of Monica Seles by a spectator obsessed with Graf. The incident was a tragedy that affected the sport and Seles deeply. Graf was not responsible for the attack.Injuries later became another challenge. Still, she found a way to finish her career on a remarkable note. Graf won her 22nd Grand Slam singles title at the 1999 French Open, defeating Martina Hingis in the final. She retired later that year, leaving behind a record that continues to inspire generations of players.Away from the tennis court, Graf built a quieter life with fellow tennis champion Andre Agassi. The couple married in 2001 and raised their two children, Jaden and Jaz. Although she no longer competes professionally, Graf has remained connected to charitable work.One of her most significant projects is Children for Tomorrow, an organisation she founded in 1998. It supports children and families affected by war, persecution and forced displacement, offering psychological help and other forms of support.Graf's life after tennis shows that an athlete's identity does not have to remain tied to competition. Her 22 major titles and Golden Slam secured her place in sporting history. Her work beyond the court adds another dimension to that legacy. At 57, her story is not one of disappearing from public life, but of choosing where to direct her time and energy.
Article Summary: Steffi Graf won 22 Grand Slam singles titles and spent 377 weeks at world No. 1. Her career brought intense pressure, public attention and difficult personal moments. After retirement, she built a life that placed family and personal priorities ahead of the spotlight. She married fellow tennis champion Andre Agassi and raised their two children.

Article Title: Ved Rahi, director of ‘Gul Gulshan Gulfam’, passes away
Article Text:
Ved Rahi





MUMBAI: Noted writer-filmmaker Ved Rahi , who directed pictures like ‘Prem Parbat’ and ‘Kali Ghata’, and the popular TV serial ‘Gul Gulshan Gulfam’, passed away at the age of 93 on Sunday.His skills as author and poet drew from a rare command over Hindi and his native Dogri.Ved Rahi was born in May 1933 in Jammu to Mulk Raj Saraf, a pioneering journalist of the state. He attained prominence as a Dogri writer in his hometown, following which he decided to move to Mumbai to test the might of his penmanship.Rahi’s success spanned over 25 films. His fame arose from having written the screenplay or dialogues of movies like ‘Yeh Raat Phir Na Aayegi’, ‘Pavitra Paapi’, ‘Aap Aaye Bahaar Aayi’, ‘Beimaan’, ‘Mome Ki Gudiya’, ‘Sanyasi’, ‘Charas’ and the sparkling ‘Bezubaan’.As his career blossomed, Rahi took the leap into direction with films like ‘Prem Parbat’ (Yeh dil aur unki nigaahon ke saaye), ‘Kali Ghata’ (Shashi Kapoor, Rekha) and recently, ‘Veer Savarkar’ in 2001. Sadly, both ‘Prem Parbat’ and ‘Kali Ghata’ are lost to viewers.Rahi was a familiar name on Doordarshan through the 1980s and 1990s thanks to serials like ‘Gul Gulshan Gulfam’, ‘Meera’, ‘Katha Sagar’, ‘Zindagi’, ‘Ehsaas’ and ‘Rishtey’.His former neighbour at New Sarvottam Society in Irla said, “He stayed here in Andheri for very long. But since many years he was with one of his two daughters. I remember that the print of his movie ‘Kali Ghata’ got destroyed in a fire. He had assisted Ramanand Sagar after he came to Mumbai. Several people from his production house bought flats in Sarvottam society.”Rahi won the Sahitya Akademi Award for his Dogri short story collection ‘Aale’ followed by the Rahul Sankrityayan Award and the Kusumagraj Rashtriya Sahitya Puraskar.He is survived by two daughters Anju Patel and Poonam Advani.
Article Summary: Rahi’s success spanned over 25 films. His fame arose from having written the screenplay or dialogues of movies like ‘Yeh Raat Phir Na Aayegi’ and ‘Pavitra Paapi’

Article Title: In AYUSH admission ‘goof-up’, students in Maharashtra allotted two seats, denied college upgrade
Article Text:
Maharashtra medical admissions: students get duplicate seat allotments (AI image)





MUMBAI: At a time when thousands of NEET aspirants are struggling to secure one medical seat, Deepali Raut* (name changed) has landed two. Both at the same homeopathy medical college in Chinchwad.She is not alone. Several AYUSH aspirants across Maharashtra have been allotted two seats, either in the same college or different institutions, following what appears to be a botched admission exercise that has left some students spoilt for choice and others deprived of a chance to upgrade to better colleges.A senior official of state CET Cell acknowledged the problem, but said little could be done at this stage, given the deadline for completing admissions.The anomalies surfaced in the third merit list released on Oct 30. Under admission rules, candidates allotted seats through the 15% quota administered by the AYUSH Admissions Central Counselling Committee (AACCC) cannot simultaneously claim seats under the 85% state quota.But an Oct 26 order from AACCC changed the equation. Candidates who had failed to secure an upgrade between rounds one and three were permitted to surrender their seats, exit central counselling and participate in the state admission process.The order came too late for the state to accommodate the cancellations before finalising its allotments. The result: candidates appearing on both lists, with some securing two seats.Parent representative and admission counsellor Kailash Tosniwal said the last-minute decision had created confusion and placed candidates in a financial bind. Those who surrender seats allotted through the central quota in private colleges risk forfeiting substantial security deposits. Reserved-category students who give up their state quota seats, meanwhile, could lose the benefit of govt fee concessions at the start of the academic year.But the bigger casualty may be students who were waiting for an upgrade.Candidates holding two allotments must surrender one seat. These seats will now become available in the fourth round, from which students already allotted seats in the first three state counselling rounds are excluded. This creates a peculiar situation: candidates with lower NEET scores who remained unallotted could secure better colleges in the fourth round, while higher-scoring students who accepted seats earlier will have no opportunity to compete for them.Had the admissions been processed in accordance with the original rules, these seats could have been available for upgrades in the third round itself, Tosniwal said, blaming AACCC for the last-minute change. For students who have played by the rules, the consequences may be difficult to accept. Some have two seats to choose from. Others have lost their chance at a better one, said Tosniwal.
Article Summary: Several AYUSH aspirants across Maharashtra have been allotted two seats, either in the same college or different institutions. The anomalies surfaced in the third merit list released on Oct 30. Under admission rules, candidates allotted seats through the 15% quota cannot simultaneously claim seats under the 85% state quota. An Oct 26 order from AACCC changed the equation.

Article Title: No time to catch their breath: Mitchell Santner flags New Zealand's recovery concerns ahead of first ODI
Article Text:
New Zealand's Mitchell Santner (AP)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner said on Tuesday that his players were feeling "a little jarred" ahead of the ODI series against India after a packed schedule that has seen the two teams play across all three formats in a little over a month.India and New Zealand are currently involved in a series comprising five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests. The hosts lost the T20I series 2-3, with the first ODI scheduled to begin on Wednesday. The 50-over matches will also help New Zealand prepare for the 2027 World Cup, while the two-Test series, starting November 19, will be important for their chances of qualifying for the World Test Championship final.The T20I series was played across four venues and ended on November 1. India played their first match within 48 hours of arriving in Auckland, leaving little time for recovery after travel."It's a very quick turnaround. With the travel and the late finishes in T20 cricket, the guys are a little bit jarred today. Recovery is a massive part of the schedule at the moment," Santner said ahead of the first ODI.The New Zealand captain said the short gaps between matches made it difficult to field the same team throughout the series, even though teams would prefer to play their strongest available XI."With one-day cricket and quick turnarounds, it can be quite taxing. You want to play your best team all the time, but with the schedules these days and the quick turnarounds, it's pretty hard to do," he added.With the 2027 World Cup less than a year away, Santner also spoke about the possibility that it could be the last ODI tournament for several members of New Zealand's ageing squad, including him. The 34-year-old said the focus could shift towards T20 cricket after the tournament."Everyone's kind of 34 or 35. With one-day cricket being in the cycle, after this World Cup, the focus is going to shift again to T20 cricket, with the T20 World Cup being the next priority as well. So, yeah, I guess no one's told me anything yet, but it could be," said the 34-year-old.Santner said rotating players would be important during the series, particularly as New Zealand look to manage workloads across formats. He also pointed to the need to build depth by giving opportunities to other players."...it creates depth, and we've seen guys coming in and stepping up straight away," he said.He added that late finishes and dew during the T20I series had made recovery more important. With the ODIs scheduled to begin at 3pm local time, he expects dew to remain a factor towards the end of the second innings."With the dew, especially in the T20s, it was quite prominent, particularly in the second innings. With a 3pm (local time) start, it's probably going to be no different towards the back end of the second innings here around the country," he said.Santner said players would have to manage their recovery based on their individual needs, with training sessions sometimes giving way to rest."Guys just have to be on top of it. Whatever it looks like...So training might look like another recovery day rather than bowling a lot."
Article Summary: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner says his players are feeling "a little jarred" ahead of the ODI series against India. India and New Zealand are currently involved in a series comprising five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests. Santner said the short gaps between matches made it difficult to field the same team.
